_comment_scenario: Qualifier-format smoke test: A is a HYPERBOLIC flyby (ECC>1, SMA<0), which is the orbit type the ranking round uses. A enters at 96,215 km (TA=-130deg), passes periapsis at 10,000 km around t=19,974s, and exits symmetrically - so T_MAX_SEC=40,000 brackets the whole flyby. Probe results (research/tools/probe_hyperbolic_A.py): propagation matches the farnocchia analytic solution to 0.002 m, Lambert converges on 3200/3200 grid points, energy floor 637.0 m/s, minimum single-burn 1257.2 m/s (under the 1500 cap, so one burn suffices). This is NOT a difficulty test - the point is that the qualifier code path had never been run end to end.
_comment_tmax: T_MAX_SEC is INVENTED. The organizers have not announced how T_max is defined for the hyperbolic ranking round (the T_max = multiple x period formula has no meaning without a period). This file proves the code path works; it says nothing about whether the number is right. Replace it when the rules are published.
_comment_scoring: k_t/C_t/k_v/C_v chosen so both terms actually move across the plausible range, per the lesson from lateral_burn_test. Fuel: 1257 m/s -> ~15.5 pts, 3000 m/s -> ~1.2 pts. Time: 10,000s -> ~20.4 pts, 35,000s -> ~6.7 pts. Sanity-check this whenever T_max changes.
